__README__: === WORKFLOW A: Loan Product Discovery (Web Crawler) === This workflow runs on a schedule (daily) and crawls public bank websites to find personal loan products. It extracts product details like interest rates, eligibility criteria, etc. and stores them in the loan_products table in PostgreSQL. HOW IT WORKS: 1. Schedule Trigger fires daily at 6 AM IST. 2. For each bank website, an HTTP Request node fetches the HTML page. 3. HTML Extract nodes pull out structured data (product names, rates, criteria). 4. A Code node normalizes the data into a consistent format. 5. A Postgres node inserts/updates the loan_products table. WHY CRAWL INSTEAD OF HARDCODE? The task says 'autonomously find and store' loan products. Hardcoding would defeat the purpose. Crawling shows you can build a real data pipeline.
name: Workflow A - Loan Product Crawler

nodes.name: Daily Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: WHAT: Fires once every day at 6:00 AM IST. WHY: The task says 'This workflow should run on a schedule (e.g., once daily).' HOW: n8n's Schedule Trigger node. It checks the time using the GENERIC_TIMEZONE env var we set in docker-compose.yml (Asia/Kolkata). WHAT IT OUTPUTS: An empty item (just a trigger signal). The next nodes do the actual work.

nodes.name: Fetch Bajaj Finserv Page
nodes.notes: WHAT: Downloads the HTML of Bajaj Finserv's personal loan page. WHY: We need the raw HTML to extract loan product information. HOW: HTTP Request node makes a GET request and returns the full HTML as text. IMPORTANT: We use responseFormat='text' so we get raw HTML, not parsed JSON. The HTML Extract node (next) needs the raw HTML string to work with.

nodes.name: Fetch HDFC Bank Page
nodes.notes: WHAT: Downloads HDFC Bank's personal loan page HTML. WHY: Second data source for loan products. We need 2-3 sites as per the task.

nodes.name: Fetch ICICI Bank Page
nodes.notes: WHAT: Downloads ICICI Bank's personal loan page HTML. WHY: Third data source. The task says 'you can choose 2-3 relevant sites'.

nodes.name: Normalize & Structure Product Data
nodes.notes: WHAT: Converts crawled data into a standardized format matching our DB schema. WHY: Different banks present data differently. This ensures consistency. OUTPUTS: One n8n item per loan product, each with all the fields our loan_products table needs.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO loan_products (product_name, provider, interest_rate, min_income, max_income, min_credit_score, max_credit_score, employment_types, min_age, max_age, source_url, last_crawled)
VALUES (
  '{{ $json.product_name }}',
  '{{ $json.provider }}',
  {{ $json.interest_rate }},
  {{ $json.min_income }},
  {{ $json.max_income }},
  {{ $json.min_credit_score }},
  {{ $json.max_credit_score }},
  ARRAY[{{ $json.employment_types.map(t => "'" + t + "'").join(',') }}]::TEXT[],
  {{ $json.min_age }},
  {{ $json.max_age }},
  '{{ $json.source_url }}',
  NOW()
)
ON CONFLICT (product_name) DO UPDATE SET
  interest_rate = EXCLUDED.interest_rate,
  min_income = EXCLUDED.min_income,
  max_income = EXCLUDED.max_income,
  min_credit_score = EXCLUDED.min_credit_score,
  max_credit_score = EXCLUDED.max_credit_score,
  employment_types = EXCLUDED.employment_types,
  min_age = EXCLUDED.min_age,
  max_age = EXCLUDED.max_age,
  last_crawled = NOW();

nodes.name: Upsert Products to PostgreSQL
nodes.notes: WHAT: Inserts each loan product into the loan_products table. If it already exists (same product_name), it UPDATES the row instead. WHY UPSERT (INSERT + ON CONFLICT UPDATE): The crawler runs daily. On day 1, products are inserted. On day 2+, they're updated with any changed criteria (like interest rate changes). Without ON CONFLICT, we'd get duplicate rows or errors. HOW n8n EXPRESSIONS WORK: {{ $json.product_name }} refers to the 'product_name' field of the current item flowing through the workflow. $json always points to the current item's data. IMPORTANT: You must set up a PostgreSQL credential in n8n with the connection details from docker-compose.yml: host=postgres, port=5432, db=clickpe_db, user=clickpe_user, password=clickpe_pass.
